title: Health Psychology Adventure 2: Addiction
welcome_lead: Today you'll explain addiction from biological, cognitive and sociocultural angles.

final_note: You explained three approaches to addiction across biological, cognitive and sociocultural levels.

concepts.def: More drug needed for same effect

walkthroughs.body_html:
All addictive drugs raise dopamine in the mesolimbic pathway (VTA → nucleus accumbens).

Repeated use causes neuroadaptation — tolerance and withdrawal.

Volkow et al. (2007): reduced D2 receptor density in addicts predicts continued use. Genetic vulnerability: heritability ~50% (Goldman et al., 2005).

Marlatt (1985) cognitive-behavioural model: outcome expectancies (the drug will relax me) guide use.

'Abstinence violation effect' — one lapse triggers full relapse via 'I've failed' thinking.

Treatment: CBT and relapse prevention rebuild expectations and coping strategies.

Peer use, family modelling, availability, advertising and poverty all raise risk.

Robins (1974): 88% of US soldiers addicted to heroin in Vietnam did not relapse on return home — context matters.

Bruce Alexander's Rat Park (1981): isolated rats consumed morphine; enriched social rats did not.
